production_note: The A baseline, B peak layer, and optional C key-art role are approved as project-level Working art direction. The review images remain non-runtime direction references and do not replace any character or mecha identity master.

assets.review_note: User approved A as the sustainable baseline language for dialogue, ordinary story art, unit illustration and runtime-facing production. This generated frame is a direction reference, not a Jicun, Guardian Z or scene master.
User approved B as the same-language peak layer for investigation, machine-spirit, terminal takeover, cut-ins and chapter visuals. It must remain switchable, area-limited and text-free.
User approved C only as an optional high-cost direction for posters, collection cards, major memories and limited story illustrations. It is not the default dialogue or sprite pipeline.
User rejected the result: it only unifies generic gacha-game rendering parameters and does not establish a distinct project art style. Retain as a failure reference.
User rejected the result: reducing panel lines and product highlights did not materially improve the mecha art. The image remains a generic catalog-style robot render.
Winged-state readability trial only. It does not grant Guardian Z permanent flight capability or replace lifecycle-specific runtime sprites.
Adult age, face, silhouette, and simplified costume direction accepted. A transparent production master and derived views are still required before Canon visual-lock migration.
Adult-coded Q direction accepted. Rebuild from the final standard master after identity lock; this review image is not a runtime sprite.

The third exploration image is the strongest of the current set, but the mecha design lacks an ownable silhouette, toy play features, and lead-mecha product appeal. Redesign from an intact C01E02 base body before deriving lifecycle variants.
Do not refine this Q asset independently. Derive it from the approved collector master and game-standard simplification.
User selected A as the superior baseline for protagonist mass and crown identity. Its gun-like forearm rails, retro color balance and surface treatment still require modernization.
Controlled B refinement. Removes gun-like forearm rails, strengthens the head, simplifies chest shutters and lower-body surface noise while preserving the five product hooks.
User likes C's modern direction but finds it too slender. Retain only its color restraint and contemporary plane organization; do not use its body mass as the lead-mecha baseline.

Current working recommendation. Preserves C's contemporary restraint while restoring head scale, chest depth, forearm weight and grounded super-robot stance without reviving gold trim or cabinet-door styling.
Uses the D design as a 2D graphic animation/game-art treatment to separate mecha-design feedback from rendering-style feedback.
First C-primary/A-mass fusion. Modern color blocking and mechanisms hold, but the generated body remains closer to C's lean proportion than requested.
Modern and heavier than C, but still lacks A's required protagonist mass and weakens the crown into a rounder generic head read.
User rejected H as ugly. It mislocated novelty in a starburst-like crown while leaving the body generic; do not use as a design parent.
User rejected I together with H. The blunt crown remained oversized and disconnected from the unchanged generic body; do not use as a design parent.

User confirmed that the face and forearms communicate the Mazinger projection, but the helmet lacks protagonist architecture and the whole machine remains old-fashioned, plain and easy to dismiss as uninteresting. Do not derive production assets from J.

User explicitly restored K as the hard upper-body parent after rejecting v8. Preserve its deep torso, paired red chest clasp, huge navy C shoulders and heavy punch mass. K itself still has non-mirrored forearm red blocks, so v9 must correct arm symmetry without redesigning the upper body.

Corrects K's oversized arcs and arm mismatch. Stronger action identity and exact mirrored punch pods; the full-body head reads well, but isolated head inspection reveals too many side and rear helmet layers.

User explicitly selected this complete helmet as the hard head base. Preserve the navy crown, red inset, face, ear interfaces and rear plates. Its antenna hierarchy is now refined by the v9W head sheet: broad main brow plus exactly two short auxiliary antennae.

Deliberate simplification control. Removing all side structure collapses the head into a round cap with a brow bar, reproducing the user's plain and uninteresting failure mode. Do not use as a design parent except as N's lower complexity boundary.

Keeps L's authored body and mirrored punch system while balancing its helmet between the layered L upper bound and plain M lower bound. Its crown is cleaner, but the upper silhouette remains somewhat smooth and rounded, so P supersedes it as the current recommendation.

Proves that dark structural side crowns can create a memorable silhouette without gold horns, but the two vault shells rise too high and read as animal horns or insect mandibles. It defines the upper silhouette bound and is not a production parent except for controlled reduction into P.

P was a useful v8 body parent, but the user subsequently restored K as the hard upper-body parent for v9. P now remains historical proportion and clean-color evidence only; its head is also superseded by the user-selected L base.
Useful v7 evidence, but no longer the active head direction after the user selected the L helmet base. The v9W head sheet resolves the requested antenna refinement.

Rejected after user correction. The four-wedge torso X replaced K's paired red clasp, the upper body lost its distinctive thickness, and the red-white treatment was incorrectly assigned to the true shoulder armor. Only the below-pelvis proportion, hinge logic and sparse marking density may be referenced.
The upturned clamp ends explain folding too literally and read as key teeth or mechanical antlers. Body remains the Q common body; antenna is rejected.

Historical antenna experiment only. The overlapping blades were unstable across views, and its Q-derived upper body was subsequently rejected for losing K's chest clasp and mass. Do not use as a production parent.
Superseded after the user requested the selected broad-brow head plus exactly two small auxiliary antennae. The pivot-bar experiment remains historical evidence only.

Rejected by user. Although the long legs and equal punch arms were useful, the Q-derived body erased K's upper-body identity and split the red chest clasp into generic X wedges. Marking positions remain candidate only; GZ-01 never established Canon numbering.
A single catalog notch adds ownership but creates a key-tooth silhouette and weakens the clean heroic head. Reject; neither U nor T is inherited by the v9 dual-auxiliary-antenna direction.

First v9 correction restores K's chest clasp, navy C shoulders and upper-body weight while lengthening only the lower body. The red shoulder-front plates remain too upright and shield-like, so V is a structural intermediate rather than the current recommendation.

The user judged W basically close to the target and retained it as the hard visual parent, then explicitly requested three controlled structural upgrades: faceted broken-frame shoulders, three large rotary-seal collar segments and one lower-body notch echo. X is now the active Candidate; W remains its identity and proportion parent.

Preserves the user-selected complete helmet and broad main brow, then adds exactly two short subordinate auxiliary antennae behind the central crown. The hierarchy is inspired by modern layered antenna design without copying Zeta Gundam's exact V-fin or head silhouette.

Current v10 Candidate. Preserves W's selected head, thick upper body, red chest clasp, long load-bearing legs and equal giant punch arms while changing only three structural motifs. The red shoulder-front end currently reads as a distinct latch block rather than a fully seamless tongue, so that connection remains an explicit review gate.
Standing mechanism evidence only. It does not replace the C01E01 half-kneeling display pose required by current story authority.
Visualizes a restrained activation change only; it does not establish a new power, wing, defense system or transformation.
Visualizes the existing rocket-punch unlock on the original right forearm. The forearm remains the same giant navy-red punch module and is not replaced by a drill, cannon or new weapon.

Shows only the C01E03 story result: the original right fist and forearm are gone, the right upper arm remains and the return interface is burned. Touring and successor right-arm designs are deliberately excluded.

Final deterministic composite built from four accepted state images. It replaces a discarded single-pass sheet whose third panel invented a gray drill and whose fourth panel added false pelvis damage. No Canon or Hard visual-lock promotion is implied.

Retained as the first shared side/rear scale study. The user confirmed its side proportion, while its broad sealed rear half and the later V12YR stretched correction are both superseded by the V13Z W-body rear.

The user confirmed this strict side proportion. It remains the side-view parent for the V13Z W-body rear resynthesis; the rejected V12YR rear spine and propulsion-frame language are not inherited. The far arm naturally overlaps the near arm in orthographic profile and does not alter the intact equal-arm engineering state.

Superseded after user review. The rear torso reads too broad, the large hubs and outward scapular covers make a wall-like back, the sealed archival spine cannot accept the established propulsion frame, and the bare body has no attitude-control nozzles. V12YR then overcorrected into a stretched back; V13Z is the current rear candidate.

Rejected by the user. Although narrower than V11Y, the long visible H spine stretches the upper back and no longer reads as the rear of the short, thick W body. Retained only as a diagnostic of the wrong vertical organization.

Rejected by the user. The two long cylindrical engines read as aviation hardware, lack lead-mecha authority, and do not reuse Guardian Z's broken-frame, red lock-plate or three-segment punch language. Retained only as a mount-load diagnostic.

Returns the rear to W/X proportions: upper-body height is compact, the wide scapular mass tapers quickly into a high narrow waist, and the nine-head ratio comes from the legs rather than a stretched spine. Its four-nozzle reading is superseded by the v14 eight-vernier rear, while this image remains the short-thick body parent.

Historical candidate. The user clarified that small posture-control nozzles belong to the bare body, while the detachable large flight pack should inherit the Mazinger-family giant-wing silhouette. The whole-body-punch equipment concept therefore no longer leads the propulsion design.

The bare body now carries eight clearly recessed posture-control nozzles: two upper-back, two rear-waist and four calf units. Shallow gold torso and foot slots remain passive heat vents. This preserves the W/X short-thick rear and does not grant normal flight.

Rejected by the user. The broad red boards plus two thin upright stabilizers read as clumsy and faintly comic from the front. The propulsion layering remains valid, but the wing silhouette is superseded by the v15 front-view variants.

The mount fit, W-body proportion and compact carrier remain useful engineering evidence, but the user rejected the broad-board and upright-fin wing silhouette. Retained only as a rear fit reference for the v15 redesign.

The rear-three-quarter view still provides useful squat-thruster and clamp-depth evidence, but its wing silhouette is rejected. Both intact original forearms remain an engineering comparison only, not a formal C01E04 state.

The user judged the completed v16E2 four-wing set inferior to this simpler twin-wing silhouette. V15A is now the hard equipment parent: exactly one continuous main wing per side, with v17 testing a commanding giant bow and a coordinated modern streamline without restoring extra wing pairs.

The folding-toy mechanism is highly legible, but the giant hinge and long down-folded panels read like a second pair of mechanical arms rather than wings. Retained as a useful diagnostic, not a recommended finalist.
This has the greatest scale and pressure, but the long open loops read as giant frame arms or architectural arches and do not communicate flight naturally. Retained as a diagnostic upper bound.

The split-arrow mechanism remains a useful Guardian-Z identity reference, but the user's later comparison reselected V15A's immediate twin-wing read as the current hard parent. It is no longer an active full-set direction.
This open-X concept produced the v16E2 mechanism set, but the user later judged the entire four-wing result inferior to V15A's twin wings. It remains only as traceable design history.

Rejected after review. Despite coherent vector-jet roots, collars and thrust channels, the front still reads as four orderly engineering appendages and loses the immediate heroic twin-wing silhouette of V15A.

The standalone mechanism remains internally coherent, but its parent four-wing visual direction was rejected as inferior to V15A. Retained only as a mechanism record, not a current equipment candidate.
The rear fit and propulsion hierarchy remain useful engineering evidence, but the user rejected the four-wing design direction. It cannot lead the next equipment pass.

The commanding extreme keeps V15A's exact twin-wing count but replaces the flat horizontal boards with one monumental tensioned bow. It tests maximum scale, weight and pressure; the primary risk is an arch or giant-scythe read at the downturned tips.

The user later identified that the A3 complete mount replaced Guardian Z's independent navy C-shaped shoulder armor. The full mounted image is rejected, but its scarlet S-curve and navy concave lower-wing geometry remain the wing-only parent for the v21 A-structure hybrid.
Rejected by the user. The separate lower vanes looked small and cheap, weakened the one-pair A3 hierarchy and did not provide sufficient residual-flight mass after main-wing removal.
Rejected by the user. The two huge circular nozzles widened the back, read as aviation engines or eyes, and did not match the intended modern Mazinger-line flight-pack power.
Rejected by the user. The wings changed shape and locked to the forearms, while the requirement is an unchanged full-size wing shell that fits over the clenched fist and leaves a visible wrist gap.
Retained as failure evidence. The mechanism intent was clearer than v18, but ivory edging, framed nozzles and straight layered parts replaced the defining A3 curvature.
Rejected. The ivory border and straighter lower layer turned the integrated S-wing into a retro three-stripe toy silhouette.
Rejected. Symmetric red backpack boxes and gold-framed square nozzles created a dated, overly regular rear design.
Rejected. The weapon still read ambiguously as a different blade or forearm attachment instead of the unchanged wing shell fitted over the fist.
Retained as the standalone view of the rejected v19 complete pack.
Retained as evidence that residual flight needs mass, but its straight secondary-wing language did not preserve the A3 curve.
Rejected by the user. The restored A3 curve was useful, but the wing-root rings occupied the shoulder axis and removed the independent navy C-shaped true shoulder armor required by the A/WX body.
Retained as rear mechanism history only. A new rear cannot be derived until the v21 mount preserves the independent shoulder armor and routes the backpack bridge behind it.
The same-part fist-cradle idea remains reusable, but this action asset inherits the rejected v20 shoulder and backpack relationship and cannot serve as the current production parent.
The standalone pack keeps useful A3 wing geometry, but its center and root architecture must be rebuilt around a short bridge behind the preserved C-shaped shoulder armor.
The residual navy-arc concept is kept as a shape reference only. It cannot advance until the v21 shoulder-preserving mount and revised standalone backpack are approved.

Current structural candidate. It keeps the complete A/WX navy C-shaped shoulder armor and red shoulder-front plate in front, while moving the backpack bridge and A3 S-curved wing roots behind the shoulders. Only this front relationship is being reviewed before any rear, standalone or attack derivatives are generated.
